findings.source_quote: ἄλλως δὲ οὐδ’ ἂν τέκνον ἢ ἀδελφὸς ἢ φίλος ἢ ἄλλως πως ποτὲ γένους μοι ἀνήκων, ἐάνπερ ἀνάξιος ᾖ, τοῦδε μὴ μεταδοῦναι χάριν, ὡς οὐ προσῆκεν.
findings.english_quote: Otherwise, not even a child or a brother or a friend or anyone in any other way ever related to me, if indeed he is unworthy—for this one’s sake not to pass it on, since it is not proper.
findings.issue: The English reproduces the fragmentary construction but assigns an unestablished relationship: “for this one’s sake” identifies τοῦδε with the unworthy person and connects it to χάριν across μὴ μεταδοῦναι. The supplied Greek does not securely establish that grouping or antecedent. Another possibility is that τοῦδε supplies the partitive object of μεταδοῦναι, referring to the material being transmitted, while χάριν expresses a favor or motive. The relation of οὐδ’ ἂν and the nominative persons to the subsequent infinitive also remains unresolved. The source_issues disclosure appropriately acknowledges uncertainty, but disclosure does not validate the chosen English construction. This is a syntactic and meaning block, not demonstrated corruption of the independently image-checked print.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the publication block while obtaining a supported syntactic analysis of the verified wording, especially οὐδ’ ἂν, the role and antecedent of τοῦδε, and the attachment of χάριν. Explicitly evaluate a partitive interpretation of τοῦδε and a favor-related interpretation of χάριν against the draft’s person-reference interpretation. Do not silently insert a governing verb, change the Greek, or present either interpretation as settled. Any resulting replacement must preserve remaining uncertainty and undergo fresh review.
